name: Will refinishing make my oak cabinets look completely smooth, or will the wood grain still show?

mainEntity.name: Will refinishing make my oak cabinets look completely smooth, or will the wood grain still show?

acceptedAnswer.text: A smooth finish is possible on many wood cabinets, but open grain, routed details, and existing surface damage affect the result. Context: “Smooth” can mean uniform color and touch, or it can mean no visible wood pores; those are different expectations. Grain filling adds labor and may change the character of the doors. Key factors: - Oak and other open-grain woods may retain texture without grain filler. - Raised panels and decorative profiles will still show their shape. - Strong side lighting can reveal sanding marks or uneven film build. Practical guidance: Define whether you want smooth color, smooth touch, or a fully grain-filled appearance. Review a sample under the same lighting used in the kitchen. Elite Remodeling & Design can align finish expectations with the chosen design style and surrounding materials.
acceptedAnswer.description: Refinishing can create an even color and finish, but open-grain wood may still show texture unless the grain is filled. Ask for a sample and clarify whether you want smooth color, smooth touch, or a fully grain-free appearance.
